Visit note | 2025-02-10 11:00 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Arafat Munshi, 33, male. Mr. Munshi comes in stating he gets breathless on the stairs, has brittle nails, and feels people notice he looks pale. He mentions these symptoms started after a stomach illness during a stay in Rangpur. He works as a restaurant cook, standing for long shifts, and lives with his brother. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies chest pain, dizziness at rest, or blackouts. On examination: haemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, BP 123/74 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 65 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and nail beds show koilonychia. Chest is clear and heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 11:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Tuhin Faruque, 22, male. Mr. Faruque reports being troubled by marks left after pimples and spots on his back. He explains the breakout flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Cox's Bazar. He works as a hotel receptionist and shares a mess in Uttara. He has no known comorbidity. He reports no fever or deep painful cysts elsewhere. On examination: about 17 inflamed spots on the face, BP 126/71 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 64 kg. Skin shows post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and active papules. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 11:30 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Tamanna Uddin, 29, female. Ms. Uddin complains of brittle nails and getting breathless on the stairs. She notes this was noticed after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Motijheel. She works as a restaurant cook and has a busy schedule. She has no chronic medical conditions. In addition, she describes a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue with little tiredness. On examination: haemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, BP 129/77 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 88 kg. Pallor is noted on the palms, and her tongue appears smooth. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 11:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Dalia Awal, 22, female. Ms. Awal presents with concerns about acne and extra hair on the face. She states this was noticed after a friend in Gulshan suggested testing. She works as a fisherman and spends long hours outdoors. She has Bronchial asthma. She denies pelvic pain or severe weight fluctuations. On examination: BMI 29.0, BP 131/82 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 71 kg. Mild hirsutism is observed along the jawline. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 12:30 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Imtiaz Gazi, 28, male. Mr. Gazi attends for review, reporting that his symptoms are worse when lying down, along with a sour taste in the mouth and burning behind the breastbone after meals. He states this has been worse since a job change in Khulna meant late heavy dinners. He works as a construction worker. He has no comorbid conditions. He denies swallowing difficulty or vomiting blood. On examination: BMI 27.2, BP 134/74 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 55 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 12:30 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Asif Mondal, 27, male. Mr. Mondal describes gritty burning eyes, long hours of screen time, and notes that symptoms are worse in air conditioning. He mentions this has been worse since moving to a new air-conditioned office in Tejgaon. He works as a restaurant cook and uses digital screens frequently. He has no chronic systemic illness. He denies eye discharge or sudden loss of vision. On examination: tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 116/84 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 77 kg. Corneas are clear with mild conjunctival injection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 03:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Mahfuz Sarkar, 21, male. Mr. Sarkar explains he has had a cough for one to two weeks after a cold and no high fever. He mentions it began after a family wedding in Motijheel. He is a university student living in a hall. He has no comorbidities. During the encounter, he reports a hoarse voice as the main complaint with only occasional cough. On examination: temperature 99.9°F, BP 118/85 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, SpO2 95%, weight 60 kg. Throat is mildly congested, and chest is clear on auscultation. Assessment: Acute bronchitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink warm fluids, use steam inhalation twice daily, and avoid smoke. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the cough continues.

Visit note | 2025-02-10 03:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Saiful Haque, 44, male. Mr. Haque reports pain when walking and a twisted ankle. He explains he twisted it while stepping off a bus in Mohammadpur. He works as an architect. He has Essential hypertension. He denies any head injury or loss of consciousness during the fall. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 136/92 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 50 kg. Lateral ligament of the right ankle shows tenderness and moderate swelling with stable joint tests. Visit note | 2025-02-10 04:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Priya Mitra, 48, female. Ms. Mitra complains of being unable to raise her arm, being unable to reach behind her back, and experiencing night pain in the shoulder. She states this began after a minor fall at home in Tejgaon. She works as an electrician. She has no other medical conditions. She denies neck pain or sensory loss in the arm. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 85 degrees, BP 136/81 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 67 kg. Active and passive range of motion is restricted in all directions. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-02-11 11:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Anjali Sen, 23, female. Ms. Sen presents with fever and sharp chest pain on breathing in. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.
